texts: Whisper not "tomorrow" to the restless hour, for what the heart means to do, let it do now before the moment slips by.

Write me a doha for someone who keeps putting off the one important task on their list, reminding them that what is meant for tomorrow should be started this very hour, before the chance quietly leaves.
need a doha that kicks me to start my assignment right now instead of tomorrow lol
do it now
I have been telling my sister for two years that I will call our estranged uncle next week, and last night she said, you have said next week since 2022.
Compose a Kabir style couplet that says what you plan to do tomorrow you should do today, and what you plan today you should do this moment, since delay slowly eats the best intentions of anyone.
Tomorrow is a promise made by the idle, O friend; today alone is in thy hand, so use it.
doha pls: stop delaying, do it today. i always say ill start monday and never do
My gym membership has run for eleven months and I have been three times, always planning to begin properly next week, and my wife just stared at me when I said it again.
today, not tomorrow
I keep telling myself I will study tomorrow and then tomorrow comes and I do nothing, so write a doha that tells me what is to be done later must be done now, no more waiting.
My father wanted to apologise to his brother for a decade, always when the right occasion came, and the right occasion never did, which I think about whenever I put off a hard conversation.
The hour of "someday" never arrives; only the step taken now makes a beginning.
plz write something about stop procrastinating, like just begin
begin today
At the crossroads of my career I kept telling my friend I'd decide after the holidays, and a swan paddling on the pond nearby seemed to say it never waits for the perfect season.
crossroads, swan, act now
doha w a swan and a crossroads, about doing it today and not waiting for tomorrow
At the crossroads the swan chooses and glides on; tomorrow's shore is never reached by those who linger.

Write a Kabir style doha where a traveller stands dithering at the crossroads while a swan has already set off across the water, teaching that what must be done should be done now before the chance is gone.
I kept saying I would tell my mother I loved her next time we spoke, but my tongue stayed tied for years, and now I do not want to wait one more call.
Please write a doha about the tongue that postpones kind words and sayings until tomorrow, reminding us to speak what is in the heart today because the moment for it passes quicker than we think.
doha about saying it today, my tongue freezes whenever i want to say sorry
tongue, say it now
O tongue, why delay the sweet word? Speak this hour, for the hush of tomorrow may keep it forever.
The lotus opens when the light calls, not when it chooses to; so open thy heart this day, not tomorrow.
lotus, now not later
Write a doha in which the lotus does not wait for a better morning to bloom but opens with the first light, teaching the one who always postpones his work to start this very day.
doha about a lotus blooming as soon as light touches it, no delay. i need that energy for my project
My teacher once pointed at the lotus pond in our school and said the flowers don't ask whether tomorrow will be better, they just open, and I still put off my homework.
stop postponing
My brother has been saying for nine years that he will finish his half-written novel when life gets calmer, and last month he turned forty.
doha on not putting things off til later pls, i have a bad habit
I want a doha in the Kabir spirit which says that tomorrow is uncertain but today is in our hands, so whatever good we plan to do, do it at once, because delay is the enemy of every plan.
What the heart says tomorrow, the hands must do now; for the hour that is spent can never be asked back.
I have owed my friend a visit for four years because I was always busy, and last week he moved abroad, so now I tell everyone to stop saying later.
Write a couplet on how people say they will do good deeds later, when they have time, yet life flows on and the chance disappears, so the wise act while they are able to.
never later
Say not "later" to the open hour, for she turns her face from the one who hesitates.
doha pls. do the thing today not later, my to-do list is a graveyard
Write a doha where a man walks through the market meaning to buy what he needs tomorrow, kicks a stone, and finds that tomorrow the chance is gone, so what is to be done must be done now.
At the market I saw a woman put back a good price on cloth saying she'd come tomorrow, and later a stone fell on the stall and it was all closed, so now I don't postpone anything.
In the market of days the bargain is struck now; tomorrow the stone is in the path and the stall is gone.
doha idea market and stone, if u dont buy it today its gone, i mean act on things now
market, stone, now
doha with a crow and a lion about doing today what you want to do, the crow just acts while the lion thinks too long
The crow seizes the morsel while the lion ponders; do your deed this hour, for hesitation starves.
My manager mulled over the proposal for months like a lion circling, while a smaller rival like a crow just grabbed the client the same afternoon.
crow, lion, act now
Write a doha in which the crow does at once what it intends, while the lion sits and postpones his hunt until the day is gone, teaching that action today beats strength with delay.
leaf, oil press, now
My uncle at the oil press told me the leaf that falls today will not rise tomorrow, so I should send my application before the deadline instead of tinkering with it forever.
doha with a leaf and an oil press about doing the work now not later, thx
The oil press turns, a leaf drifts down; what is yours to do will not wait on the wind of tomorrow.
Write a doha about the oil press that must be run today to get oil, and the fallen leaf that cannot go back up, showing that tasks postponed are lost and work should be done now.
The loom waits not for the weaver's mood; one row woven today is worth a hundred he will promise tomorrow.
weaver's loom, start now
doha about weaver's loom and not delaying the work, i need to stop saying tomorrow
Compose a doha in which the weaver sits at his loom the very moment the light comes, never saying he will begin tomorrow, so that a procrastinating mind may learn to start the work now.
My grandfather sat at his loom every dawn without fail and used to say a day he put off was a day's weaving lost, and that is why I now open my laptop at six.
The hour that is now is the only hour that is ours; the rest is only a promise.
My friend kept saying he would propose to his girlfriend after the next promotion, and then the next, and she finally married someone who asked sooner.
today is yours
Please write a doha for a young person who keeps saying they will start life properly once everything is perfect, reminding them that the perfect moment never comes and today is the only time given.
can u gimme a doha on how u should do stuff now cuz later never comes
doha with a thief and a crossroads, the thief of time is putting stuff off, i keep losing days
crossroads, thief of time
At the crossroads waits the thief called "Later", and he steals the hours of those who linger.
I stood at the crossroads of two job offers for three weeks saying I'd decide tomorrow, until both were given away, and my brother said delay is a quiet thief.
Write a doha where the thief waits at the crossroads and steals from every traveller who lingers, teaching that procrastination robs us of the day and what must be done should be done at once.
Write me a doha about a man who constantly says I will start saving, I will start exercising, I will start learning, and never does, and show that what is done now is worth more than a hundred plans.
something short like a doha on starting right now. been procrastinating on my taxes for weeks
start now or never
Plans are only breath unless they are begun; leave nothing to the later hour, but do it now.
My mother has had a lump on her arm checked for six months because she keeps saying it can wait till after my cousin's wedding, and I want her to go this week.
Write a doha where the heron watches the shallows while the net hangs idle, and the owner says he'll cast it tomorrow, teaching that opportunity passes and work delayed is work lost.
The heron strikes at once, the net lies folded; the one who says "tomorrow" gathers only empty water.
My uncle's net stayed untouched in the shed all week while he said the heron was no threat to his pond, and by Saturday the pond was empty.
doha with a heron and a net about acting today, not waiting around
heron, net, act now
doha for me, i keep telling myself ill call my mom later, then forget
Last Diwali I told my father I would visit for the weekend after my deadlines, and then the deadlines kept coming, and now I've decided to take the next bus.
do good today
Kind deeds fade by evening, so gather them this morning, ere the hour forgets.
Write a doha reminding us that kindness and goodness we intend to show others should be shown today, since the hour of chance passes quickly and no one is promised another.
I kept pushing off the hem on my daughter's dress, saying I'd stitch it tomorrow, and the day of the school function came with a loose thread and no time at all.
Compose a doha in which a single loose thread, left alone until tomorrow, pulls apart the whole cloth, so that a small task postponed grows large and the sensible mend it at once.
thread, do it now
doha w thread in it about not delaying, like fix the small thing now before it unravels
One loose thread, mended today, saves the garment; left for tomorrow, it unravels the whole weave.
Write a Kabir style doha for a student who has months to prepare but spends each day in leisure thinking there is plenty of time, then panics at the end, reminding him to begin now.
I once watched my cousin leave his thesis for the last fortnight, working through five nights without sleep, and now I begin even the dull tasks on the first day.
no delay
doha on starting early, deadline stress is killing me
The long day of "plenty of time" ends in a hurried dusk; begin while the morning is still young.
doha with scales and about doing good things right now, the scales of time tip and then its too late
Write a doha in which the scales weigh each day exactly the same, and the one who puts off his work for tomorrow finds the balance tilted against him, for time once gone is never regained.
The scales of the hours tip quickly, O friend; what you hold back for tomorrow is already weighed and lost.
scales, now not later
The scales my grandmother used to weigh lentils grew a little off each season as she kept postponing getting them fixed, and I realize now she lost money on every sale.
doha w a blind man in it - the one who keeps delaying is like him, cant see time slipping away
blind man, wasted days
The blind man cannot see the hours pass, nor can the one who says "tomorrow"; both walk past their chance.
I helped an old blind man cross the street this morning and he said, nothing waits for me, son, so do what you can today, which made me feel awful about my pending work.
Write a doha comparing the person who always postpones to a blind man who cannot see how quickly the days are passing, and urging that what is worth doing be done this very day.
The moneylender counts his diamond twice but never sells; wise is he who spends the hour today.
My uncle, a moneylender, kept a diamond locked away waiting for a better price for years, and when he finally went to sell, prices had crashed, so I act at once now.
Write a doha about a moneylender who hoards his diamond and says he will make use of it tomorrow, but the day never comes, teaching that value unused today is wasted and good deeds delayed are lost.
moneylender, diamond, now
doha w a moneylender and a diamond: use what u have today, dont wait for a perfect time
My grandfather always said he would build us a palace of a home someday, and he died with only the plan in his pocket, so I am beginning my own small life right now.
Write a doha about a king who keeps promising a palace to his people tomorrow, yet never lays one brick, teaching that action now is worth more than a grand plan postponed again and again.
palace of tomorrow
doha about a palace people dream of but never start building, i wanna do things now
A palace dreamed on tomorrow's soil rises not; one brick laid today is worth a thousand sighs.
can u write a doha on do it now, im a chronic procrastinator
I would like a doha to put up on my wall that tells me whatever work is waiting should be done at this moment, without excuses, because the one who keeps delaying ends with nothing in his hands.
now, now, now
The present moment waits at thy threshold; welcome him with deeds, for he will not knock twice.
Every New Year I make a list of resolutions that I tell myself I will start from the next month, and by December nothing has changed, and my wife has stopped asking.
doha w a bridge: build it today, dont wait or the gap gets wider

Write a doha about a man who delays building a bridge until the next season, and finds the water risen and the work harder, teaching that what is done now is easy and what is deferred grows difficult.
Lay the first plank of the bridge this morning, for the floods of tomorrow widen every gap.
bridge, build today
My cousin postponed patching things up with his friend until the rift felt unbridgeable, and my father said a bridge built early is a short one.
Our neighbour has been meaning to repair her relationship with her daughter since the day they argued, and she keeps waiting for the perfect moment to call, which has not come in six years.
stop delaying
doha pls, about how if u wanna do something do it right now, got a bad habit of waiting
Say not "tomorrow" to thy heart's good wish; the present hour is the only one that obeys.
Write me a Kabir doha for the lazy-minded who always have a reason to start later, explaining that whatever is to be done should be done at this very moment because the next hour is not yours.
Write a doha where the mosque call is heard at dawn and the dew is still on the ground, telling the sleeper not to wait until noon, for what must be done is best done while the morning is fresh.
doha w mosque and dew, wake up and do it now, mornings go fast
While the dew still clings and the mosque stands hushed in the dawn, rise and begin, for the noon dries all excuses.
Every morning the mosque near our building wakes the whole street while the dew is still on the grass, and my neighbour says that is when to start your work, not after lunch.
mosque, dew, begin now
Write a doha for a person who has a difficult conversation to have with someone they love and keeps delaying it, saying the best moment to make things right is now, before the distance grows wider.
My husband has been avoiding paying the electricity bill for three months because he says he'll go to the office next week, and today they cut our supply and he finally went.
doha about doing hard things first thing, not tomorrow
The hard thing delayed grows heavier by the hour; face it today while thy strength is fresh.
do the hard thing today
Why wait for the perfect season, O seeker? The deed done now is already perfect.
I wanted to start learning guitar after I got a good job, then after I moved cities, then after my wedding, and now I'm forty and have never touched one.
Please write a doha about people who wait for the perfect conditions before beginning anything, and show that the right time is always now and that the wise begin with whatever they have.
plz a doha about not waiting for perfect timing, just start
start, don't wait
doha w a sword in it: the sword rusts if u dont use it, same with ur plans, do it today
My grandfather's old sword hung on the wall unused for sixty years, rusting while he kept planning to polish it, and my father says do not let your own talents rust the same way.
sword, use it now
Write a doha about a warrior who keeps his sword sheathed until tomorrow's battle and finds it rusted, teaching that skills and good intentions must be used today or they decay with delay.
The sword that sleeps in its sheath till tomorrow wakes to rust; strike thy good work now.
O wavering heart, what is not begun now is already lost, and "tomorrow" is a promise that never keeps its word.
doha about doing stuff now, like seriously just do it
I told my kids I'd teach them chess this weekend, then the next, and last week my eldest said, Dad, you always say next time.
Compose a doha that says the person who says I will do it later is cheating himself, because the thing postponed is the thing never done, and only the work begun today bears any result.
now or never
Open the door this very hour, O friend, for the guest of opportunity does not stand outside forever.
A salesman waited outside our door for an hour yesterday while I told my wife I'll sign up for the course next week, and she said that is exactly the problem with you.
Write a doha about a door that stands open for just a short while and the man who says he will walk through tomorrow, only to find it shut, teaching that chances are used now or lost.
doha with a door - if u dont walk thru today its closed tmrw. i keep missing chances
open door, go now
The door of the old furnace room swung open and shut as the smith kept saying he'd fix the leak tomorrow, and the whole stock cooled and was spoiled by morning.
furnace, door, act now
Strike while the furnace glows and the door stands open; cold iron laughs at "tomorrow".
doha w furnace and a door, about acting when the time is hot, not later
Compose a doha in which the furnace is hot and the door is open, and the smith who postpones his hammering until tomorrow finds the metal cold, teaching that every task has its moment and it is now.
skeleton, do it now
doha w a skeleton: u keep saying later but later is just bones lol, do it now
Write a doha in which a skeleton lies where a man once said he would do good tomorrow, showing that the days of delay turn to nothing and only deeds done today are real.
At the anatomy lab our professor pointed at the skeleton and said the owner probably meant to finish many things tomorrow, so don't leave your thesis for next semester.
The skeleton keeps no calendar and no promises; whatever thou meanest to do, do it while thy hands are warm.

Write a doha where the spinning wheel keeps turning every day while the lazy man says he'll climb the mountain tomorrow, teaching that the day's work is done today and distant goals are reached by daily action.
doha w a mountain and spinning wheel, begin the climb today not someday
mountain, spinning wheel, today
My great aunt spun yarn on her wheel each day even as the mountain loomed over the village, and she told me never to put off the first step of any climb.
The spinning wheel turns today, the mountain waits for no one; take thy first step, O dreamer.
Write a Kabir doha for a young man who has a fine idea but wants to wait until he is older, richer and more skilled before he begins, reminding him that the first step is best taken today.
Not when the omens align, nor when the means are full, but when thy heart says now, begin.
My roommate has had a business idea since college, and he says he'll start when he has saved enough, while his rival with half the idea launched last month and has customers.
first step, today
doha about starting my dream project today instead of waiting till im ready
grindstone, work today
Write a doha where the grindstone must be turned each day to get flour, and the man who says he will grind tomorrow goes hungry tonight, teaching that today's work cannot be saved for later.
My mother turns the grindstone first thing every dawn and calls it a sin to leave the day's work for the next, and I still leave my dishes for the morning.
doha with a grindstone: do the days work today or the flour doesnt come, you get it
The grindstone grinds the grain of this day only; tomorrow's hunger is not fed by today's idleness.
doha: stop saying ill do it later, ive got stuff piling up
today, do it today
For two years I've said I'd get my driving licence after the busy season, and my son passed his test last week at eighteen, which made me feel quite small.
Write a doha for someone whose unfinished tasks are piling up higher every week, telling them that what is put off today doubles tomorrow and the only way to lighten the load is to start now.
The piled-up "laters" grow into a wall by evening; break the first piece of it this morning.
lion, act now
The zookeeper told us the lion sleeps most of the day, but the moment it sees something it needs, it acts without a second's delay, which I wish I could learn for my work.
Write a doha about a lion who does not say he will hunt tomorrow but springs the instant he must, teaching people who delay everything that decisive action today beats a hundred stored-up intentions.
doha with a lion: lions dont wait til tomorrow, they act. i need that vibe
The lion does not whisper "tomorrow"; he leaps, and the hour is his. So rise, O drowsy heart.
paras, use it now
doha w the paras, u hold it today but dont use it, then its gone
My grandfather had a rare skill with herbs and said he'd teach me later, and he died before he did, so I treat every chance to learn as a paras I must grab today.
The paras of the alchemists lies in thy palm this hour; touch thy work to it now, for it fades with the morrow.

Write a doha about someone who discovers the legendary paras of the alchemists but says he will use its magic tomorrow, only to lose his chance, teaching us to use every treasure of time in the present.
A thousand "tomorrows" are only one idle sigh; one deed done now is a living thing.
I told my friend I'd help him move flats on Saturday and then on Sunday and finally he hired movers, and I realised my habit of putting everything off is hurting people.
do it today
doha pls on act now stop waiting, im trying to quit being lazy about my goals
Please write a couplet for the man who is always just about to begin, telling him that the time for beginning is not later but at this moment, for the deed must be started to bear anything at all.
churn, priest, today
The priest at our village used to churn the curd himself every dawn and told the boys that if the churn is left idle till tomorrow the butter is lost, so work today.
The priest churns on, the butter gathers; leave the churn idle till tomorrow and all the day's cream is lost.

Write a doha about a priest who sits idle beside the churn and says he will begin tomorrow, teaching that spiritual or worldly gains come only from today's effort and none from promises for another day.
doha w a priest and a churn - the work isn't done unless u start churning now
Write a doha in which a man finds the paras of the alchemists and plans to use it tomorrow, but the delay turns his fortune to dust, teaching that every chance must be seized this very day.
The paras gleams in thy hand, but only the hour that is now can work its alchemy.
doha pls, about the paras, when u have a chance use it today
My uncle found an offer that could have changed his career, a real paras, but he kept saying he'd reply after the holidays, and the offer went to someone else.
paras, seize today
The palace is built brick by brick today, never by the "tomorrow" of a dreamer's sigh.
doha w a palace in it, i keep planning my dream life but never start building it

Compose a doha about a prince who dreams of a great palace and says he will lay its foundation tomorrow, though each day he delays, the dream recedes, teaching that work begun today builds all greatness.
My cousin has drawn the plans for his dream palace of a startup for ten years, and last week a school friend with half his plan launched it, so I told him to begin today.
palace, begin today
Write a doha for a person who thinks of reconciling with an old friend but waits for the friend to call first, reminding them that pride is a delay and the right moment to reach out is today.
Let not pride keep the hour: the hand extended now is warmer than the hand extended too late.
doha about calling an old friend today instead of overthinking it
It was my best friend's birthday last month and I kept saying I'd call tomorrow because I felt awkward after our fight, and now it's been four years of silence.
call them today
The milk spoils by evening when left uncared for; do thy work this morning, for the day is short.
I left the milk out on the counter saying I'd put it away after the call, and by the evening it was sour, and my wife said that's you with every task, always after.
Write a doha in which the milk must be boiled the moment it is fresh or it spoils by night, teaching a procrastinating mind that all things need doing at the proper time, which is today.
milk spoils, act now
doha with milk in it, if u dont deal with it today it goes bad, like my tasks

Write a doha about a diamond lying untouched beside a grindstone because the owner says he'll cut and polish it tomorrow, teaching that unfinished work and wasted chances do not shine until begun now.
The diamond waits unpolished beside the grindstone's rest; a gem unworked today is a pebble tomorrow.
doha w a diamond and a grindstone, you gotta polish talent now, not someday
diamond, grindstone, today
My friend's daughter has a rare singing talent like an uncut diamond, and she keeps saying she will practise seriously after her exams, and the grindstone of daily work never starts.
Write a doha that says do not wait until the shroud and sandalwood are brought to make peace with those you have wronged or do the good you intended, because what is delayed may never be done.
I waited until the day of my uncle's funeral, with the sandalwood laid beside the shroud, to apologise for our fight, and it was too late, so now I say sorry the same day.
doha w a shroud and sandalwood in it - if u wanna say sorry do it now not at the end
sandalwood, shroud, forgive today
Do not wait for the shroud and the sandalwood to speak your tender word; say it while the ears can hear.
The swan leaves the market of delay at dawn, for the day is short and tomorrow's sellers are gone.
At the market I saw a swan-necked vase for sale and the buyer said he'd come back tomorrow, and a clever man took it, which is what happens whenever I put things off.
Write a doha where the swan departs the market early before the crowd arrives because he does his business at once, while the one who delays finds the best goods gone, teaching to act now.
doha w a swan and a market - the early swan gets the good stuff, so act today
swan, market, now
My father keeps saying he will see a specialist about his heart next month, but his cough has lasted since January, and I want to drag him to the clinic today.
doha about booking that appointment today, no more postponing
Compose a Kabir style doha saying the good intentions of tomorrow are only dreams, that today alone is real, and that those who act immediately are the only ones who get anything done in life.
no more delays
Of all the hours, the best is the one that is now; let thy hand not wait on the lazy "later".
